trigger: unhappy-path (Gate 4) flagged 3 bare std::lock_guard sites inside teardown_claimed (noexcept) as a std::terminate risk if rec->mu.lock() throws; sre (Gate 6) attempted to downgrade this by citing server.cpp's S-BRIDGE-TICK-GUARD try/catch around sweep(). Orchestrator independently verified: teardown_claimed IS declared noexcept (mcp_stream_bridge.hpp:1150) and sweep() is NOT (mcp_stream_bridge.hpp:663) - an exception escaping a noexcept function calls std::terminate() at that function's own boundary, before unwinding ever reaches sweep()'s frame or the outer try/catch. sre's downgrade is correct for a DIFFERENT lock (Pass R's own claim-commit lock in sweep()'s loop, which genuinely is covered by the guard) but does not apply to the 3 sites unhappy-path actually named.
summary: A genuine mutex-lock throw inside teardown_claimed's 3 bare-lock sites (attempt bookkeeping, mark_retry_or_exhausted, the recovered counter) would std::terminate() the whole process; no fault-injection seam exists to test it; requires the same mutex-corruption fault this file already models as real but rare (E5). Original unhappy-path characterization stands; sre's attempted downgrade was reviewed and does not hold for these specific sites - see rationale.
rationale: adjudicated disagreement between Gate 4 unhappy-path and Gate 6 sre, resolved by the orchestrator via direct signature verification (noexcept on teardown_claimed, absent on sweep) rather than accepting either report at face value

trigger: under a sustained/persistent platform fault, many records could exhaust their retry budget and be permanently retained, each holding a global + per-session admission slot
summary: Compound resource-starvation risk under sustained fault; confirmed bounded by global_record_cap=256 (sre, Gate 6) - worst case is the whole fleet-wide streaming budget stranded until restart, already covered by existing RecordsNearCap/AtCapacity alerts
rationale: design tradeoff, bounded not unbounded per independent sre verification; still worth tracking as a known worst-case

trigger: Pass R runs first in sweep(), synchronously, ahead of pressure relief (passes 0+) - could delay pressure relief exactly during the pressure episode causing the retry faults
summary: Bounded by teardown_retry_max x eligible-record-count per tick, confirmed self-limiting by sre; no compound escalation found when examined jointly with F11 by chaos-injector
rationale: design ordering choice, deliberate per architect (Gate 3): real spacing invariant requires Pass R first
